rule_level_problems.problem: OR of four single morphologies where the page lists them together. 'Skin nodule' is_a 'Mass of skin', the page's presenting complaint, so almost any lump recorded as a nodule (Kaposi's lesion, boil, cyst) also becomes probable acne. Consider any2, or drop the bare Skin nodule branch.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable boil (skin lump/s) / Diagnose probable skin abscess (skin lump/s)
rule_level_problems.problem: AND of six findings including Skin discharge; a boil that has not yet pointed and discharged does not match, though the page's 'softens in the centre to discharge pus' describes the course. Fluctuant alone (with pain, firm, red, warm) would be the page's intent before discharge.

'Skin dimple' is a generic skin-surface dimpling finding standing in for umbilicated papules; with 'small papule' it is a loose signature. No better concept exists, so this is a note for the remaining-questions file rather than a fix.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: mole needing same-week referral (skin lump/s)
rule_level_problems.problem: Priority level Urgent for a page that says 'refer same week'. Consistent with the house rule that a red box becomes Urgent, but the page does not say 'urgent attention'; worth a clinician's confirmation.

'Moves easily' and 'doughy' are not encoded, so lipoma and epidermoid cyst are separated only by Soft+Painless vs Round+Firm. Probably not_representable (no mobile/doughy qualifier found) but should be recorded as a gap.

summary: The acne rule is an OR of single morphologies and 'Skin nodule' is a SNOMED child of 'Mass of skin' (the page's presenting complaint), so most lumps on this page also come out as probable acne. In the red box, 'Bleeds easily' is a systemic bleeding-tendency concept rather than bleeding from the mole, and 'Differs from surrounding moles' is not encoded at all; the other four mole criteria and the > 6 mm measurement are correct. The boil/abscess rules require all six descriptors including discharge, and several textural descriptors (pearly, skin-coloured, doughy, moves easily) are absent with no SNOMED equivalent.
